answer: Neighborhood overlap gating. Each identity advertises its peer set; admission to shared resources requires that its neighbors form a densely connected orchard of mutual links, verified by sampling. Isolated clusters get throttled because honest agents cluster around common hubs. An attacker must fabricate many interlinked identities, paying per-identity the compute to maintain those links and pass sampling, while a lone cipher account stays outside the oasis of trusted subgraphs.
